Poor customer service. I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Trip.com.

I accidentally booked an AirAsia flight for the wrong year while trying to purchase an urgent flight for my father. I realized the mistake almost immediately and contacted Trip.com within about an hour of making the booking.

I was not asking to cancel a trip that I no longer wanted. This was an honest booking error that I reported right away. Despite this, my refund request was denied, and the alternatives offered were unreasonable.

What shocked me most was that when I asked about changing the ticket, I was quoted more than 6,335 THB in additional charges to correct a booking that originally cost me around 4,015 THB. Paying more than the value of the original ticket simply to fix an obvious mistake made no sense and felt completely unfair.

Throughout the process, customer service provided little meaningful assistance. I spent time explaining the situation and asking for help, but received mostly scripted responses and no practical solution. There seemed to be no willingness to consider the fact that the mistake was reported almost immediately after booking.

I understand that companies have policies, but there should be some level of flexibility and common sense when a customer reports an obvious error within an hour of purchase. Instead, I was left with the feeling that customer support was focused on enforcing rules rather than helping customers.

This experience has seriously damaged my trust in Trip.com. Based on how my case was handled, I would strongly encourage others to be extremely careful when booking through this platform, because if you make a simple mistake, you may find yourself paying far more than expected with very little support.

reviews.text:
BUY DIRECTLY THROUGH THE AIRLINE INSTEAD. I bought round trip tickets for my girlfriend and I (4 tickets total) from trip.com that indicated 1x personal bag and 1x carry-on was allowed for each of us on the flights and that it was an “economy ticket”. My flight is today and they just gave me my boarding passes which showcase “economy light” on the ticket, which according to the airline policy only allows for 1x personal bag OR 1x carry-on. I tried to complain to their customer service rep but they were no help, saying that economy light was what I purchased. No I purchased economy and it indicated one of each on their app. I know for certain that it did. I wouldn’t have purchased any ticket if it hadn’t allowed for the proper luggage that we needed, what kind of idiot would do that. So now I am out an additional €140 to add luggage on the flights ($163.80). 

Summary: Their app was misleading (more accurately, they lied) on how much luggage was allowed with the ticket we purchased and they provided us the wrong class of ticket. We had to buy extra baggage allowance. Just book through the airline rather than trying to save a few bucks. Lesson learned and will never use them again.

reviews.text:
Disappointed but stuck. I don’t know if this will help anyone else, but just in case: I booked tickets for the wrong date- absolutely my fault. When we were made aware of this at the airport, the ticketing agent offered-very kindly-to help us get the right tickets. She said they were “transferring” our flights, but then charged us the full price of the original tickets. This was all done at the airport in Chinese and I assumed I misunderstood with my limited Chinese and that I would be able to cancel and refund part of the original tickets from Trip.com- I can not. 
After interacting with the chatbot, and then calling to speak with a service rep who “could not help,” I asked to speak with a manager who *could* help, but was just sent an email reiterating there’s nothing that can be done and did not even receive the courtesy of the promised call. Trip.com has not reflected the transfer of our tickets in the app in anyway-it still has the original flights listed ready for us to take- yet they are “unable” to refund me any part of the original price for either set of ticket. I feel stuck as there are not many foreign friendly way to buy tickets in China. 
My word of caution: don’t trust the app and the airlines to communicate in your favor. They absolutely will not. I have paid the price of two trips for one.

Not a reliable company I was left without accommodation I paid for!. I booked a fully prepaid stay through Trip.com, received confirmation, and even had confirmation from the hotel. However, upon arrival after a 24-hour international trip with my child, the hotel informed me that no reservation existed and that they were fully booked.

This left me without accommodation upon arrival in a foreign country, which is unacceptable.

Trip.com support was not able to secure alternative accommodation and instead advised me to find a hotel on my own and request reimbursement later. This placed the burden entirely on me despite having a confirmed booking.

While a refund was initiated, this does not address the stress, inconvenience, and risk caused by this situation especially while traveling with a child.

I expect booking platforms to ensure that confirmed reservations are honored or that immediate equivalent accommodation is provided when issues arise. This experience significantly undermined my trust in Trip.com.

If everything goes exactly as planned, Trip.com may be fine. But if your trip is disrupted, especially internationally, be prepared to handle resolution yourself.
